Visit note | 2025-11-22 04:00 PM | Dr. Habibur Rahman, Orthopedics | Patient: Bithi Chakraborty, 63, female. Mrs. Chakraborty comes in for her first visit reporting lower back pain after lifting something heavy, which improves with rest and causes stiffness when bending. She mentions this started after lifting sacks at a warehouse in Gazipur. She works as a madrasa teacher. Comorbidity: Hypothyroidism. She has no radiating leg pain or numbness. On examination: pain score 5/10, BP 125/72 mmHg, pulse 83 bpm, weight 79 kg. Spine movements are limited by pain. Assessment: Lumbar muscle strain. Plan: a prescription was issued. Advice: stay gently active; use a warm compress; lift with the knees bent. Follow-up in 2 weeks if the pain continues.

Visit note | 2025-11-22 04:00 PM | Dr. Mahbuba Rahman, Psychiatry | Patient: Rekha Mitra, 63, female. Ms. Mitra presents for her first visit describing a complete lack of interest in her usual activities, poor sleep, and a persistently low mood for over three weeks. She notes this started after the death of a parent in Motijheel. Her occupation is a farmer. Comorbidity: none. She denies any physical pain or sensory loss. On examination: PHQ-9 score 16, BP 131/78 mmHg, pulse 74 bpm, weight 78 kg. She appears tearful and subdued. Assessment: Depressive episode. Plan: a prescription was issued. The patient denies thoughts of self-harm, and a safety plan with the emergency number 999 was discussed. Advice: keep a daily routine; walk outdoors daily; start counselling sessions; call 999 or come to the clinic at once if thoughts of self-harm appear. Follow-up in 2 weeks.

Visit note | 2025-11-22 04:30 PM | Dr. Lubna Rahman, Endocrinology | Patient: Priya Chakraborty, 58, female. Mrs. Chakraborty returns for a review of her ongoing condition, reporting shaky hands, losing weight despite eating well, and a racing heart. This began after a stressful family event in Keraniganj. She works as a retired civil servant. Comorbidity: none. She has no heat intolerance or visual disturbances. On examination: pulse 109 bpm, BP 135/77 mmHg, weight 89 kg. Tremors are noticeable in both outstretched hands. Assessment: Hyperthyroidism. Plan: a prescription was issued. Advice: avoid excess tea and coffee; rest when the heart races. Follow-up in 4 weeks with thyroid function tests.

Visit note | 2025-11-23 10:00 AM | Dr. Moinul Haque, Neurology | Patient: Emon Dewan, 46, male. Mr. Dewan attends for a follow-up consultation regarding persistent stress and band-like pressure around his head. He explains that these symptoms began after a stressful house move to Jatrabari. He works as a police constable and has experienced several demanding shifts recently. He reports no neurological deficits, weakness, or visual disturbances. Comorbidity: none. On examination: pain score 6/10, BP 132/83 mmHg, pulse 82 bpm, weight 69 kg. Cranial nerves are intact, and muscle tone is normal throughout. Assessment: Tension-type headache. Plan: a prescription was issued. Advice given includes taking screen breaks every hour, doing neck stretches, and ensuring seven hours of sleep. Follow-up in 1 month.

Visit note | 2025-11-23 11:30 AM | Dr. Nazma Begum, Obstetrics and Gynecology | Patient: Nargis Sarkar, 44, female. Ms. Sarkar visits for the first time complaining of local soreness, persistent itching, and thick white discharge. She states this began during the humid monsoon in Bashundhara. Visit note | 2025-11-23 02:00 PM | Dr. Arif Hossain, Pulmonology | Patient: Amit Biswas, 63, male. Advice: rest and drink plenty of fluids; return at once if breathing becomes difficult. Follow-up in 3 days for review and a chest X-ray in 6 weeks.

Visit note | 2025-11-23 02:30 PM | Dr. Jannatul Ferdous, Orthopedics | Patient: Nupur Das, 48, female. Visit note | 2025-11-23 02:30 PM | Dr. Rezaul Karim, Neurology | Patient: Habib Ahmed, 60, male. Visit note | 2025-11-23 04:00 PM | Dr. Tanvir Ahmed, General Medicine | Patient: Chandana Sarkar, 62, female. She works as a madrasa teacher. Comorbidity: Bronchial asthma. She reports no bleeding manifestations so far. Follow-up in 48 hours with a repeat platelet count.

Visit note | 2025-11-24 09:30 AM | Dr. Nasrin Sultana, Gastroenterology | Patient: Anwar Faruque, 29, male. Mr. Faruque returns for review, stating that his stomach discomfort gets worse when he feels stressed, and his bowel habits continue to switch between loose stools and hard ones. He works as a delivery rider and recalls that these tummy issues began after a bout of food poisoning in Sirajganj. He reports no red flag symptoms such as weight loss or blood in the stool. Assessment: Irritable bowel syndrome. Plan: a prescription was issued today. He was advised to eat regular meals, keep a detailed food diary, and reduce tea, fizzy drinks, and beans. Follow-up in 6 weeks with the food diary.
